---
title: Build an agent app
description: Copy a host, a web app, or a terminal interface and change it from there
---

## Make an API call

```ts title="host.ts"
import { createNyteModels } from "@nyte-ai/ai";
import { SqliteStore } from "@nyte-ai/core/store";
import { createHost, resolveModel } from "@nyte-ai/host";

const models = createNyteModels();
const sdk = await createHost({
  models,
  model: await resolveModel(models, "{{model}}"),
  store: new SqliteStore("./agent.db"),
  plugins: { kind: "chat", system: "You are a helpful assistant." },
});

// Run queued messages in this process. Call once when the host starts.
sdk.attach();

const { sessionId } = await sdk.sessions.create();
await sdk.messages.send({ sessionId, content: "Hello" });
await sdk.runs.wait({ sessionId });

const snapshot = await sdk.sessions.snapshot({ sessionId });
if (snapshot === undefined) throw new Error("Session not found");

console.log(JSON.stringify(snapshot.transcript, null, 2));
```

`createHost` prepares the SDK; `attach()` enables its background runner. Creating a session and
sending a message only store data. Keeping execution separate lets a UI send messages while
another process runs the agent. In this example, the same process does both.

`snapshot` reads the session's current state, or returns `undefined` if the session no longer
exists. Its `transcript` is conversation data, not a component. `JSON.stringify` is only for
printing it here. For a live React view, use the observer in [Make a web app](#make-a-web-app).

`plugins.kind` picks which plugins the host loads: `chat` is a system prompt alone, `workspace`
adds a project folder with its tools and plugins, and `custom` takes a list you build. What a
plugin is, and where a session gets them, is in [Plugins](/docs/kernel/plugins).

To work in a project folder, switch to workspace mode:

```ts title="host.ts"
import { createHost, createWorkspaceBackend, createWorkspaceStore } from "@nyte-ai/host"; // [!code ++]

const workspaces = createWorkspaceStore(); // [!code ++]
const workspace = await workspaces.require(process.cwd()); // [!code ++]

const sdk = await createHost({
  models,
  model: await resolveModel(models, "{{model}}"),
  store: new SqliteStore("./agent.db"),
  workspace: createWorkspaceBackend(workspaces), // [!code ++]
  plugins: { kind: "chat", system: "You are a helpful assistant." }, // [!code --]
  plugins: { kind: "workspace", target: { kind: "project", workspace } }, // [!code ++]
});
```

`require()` throws until the user trusts the folder. Ask first, then call `workspaces.trust(cwd)`.
Trust lets project plugins run and gives the agent unrestricted tools in that folder. It isn't a
sandbox, and Nyte doesn't ask per tool call. To share history with the TUI and desktop app, open
the store at `workspaceStorePath(workspace.cwd)`.

## Make a web app

The SDK packages aren't on npm yet. The install commands below work once they publish under `@next`.

The host needs Node 26.4 or later. Run `nyte login` first, since the `openai-codex` provider signs in through it.

### Vite

Create a React app and install the public SDK packages:

```sh
pnpm create vite chat-web --template react-ts
cd chat-web
pnpm install
pnpm add @nyte-ai/client@next @nyte-ai/ai@next @nyte-ai/core@next @nyte-ai/host@next @nyte-ai/server@next
```

#### Run the host

This is a separate Node process, not code for Vite to bundle. It serves only the API on port 8787.

```ts title="chat-web/server.ts"
import process from "node:process";
import { createNyteModels } from "@nyte-ai/ai";
import { SqliteStore } from "@nyte-ai/core/store";
import { createHost, resolveModel } from "@nyte-ai/host";
import { serve } from "@nyte-ai/server/node";

const models = createNyteModels();
const store = new SqliteStore("./agent.db");
const sdk = await createHost({
  models,
  model: await resolveModel(models, "{{model}}"),
  store,
  plugins: { kind: "chat", system: "You are a helpful assistant." },
});
const detach = sdk.attach();

const serving = await serve({
  sdk,
  version: "0.0.16-dev.2",
  auth: { kind: "token", token: process.env.NYTE_TOKEN ?? "" },
  browserOrigins: ["http://localhost:5173", "http://localhost:3000"],
  port: 8787,
});

process.once("SIGINT", async () => {
  await serving.close();
  detach();
  await sdk.close();
  await store.close();
});
```

`serve` binds `127.0.0.1` and refuses a token shorter than 16 characters. `attach()` runs queued
messages in this process; serving the API alone does not execute them.

From `chat-web`, generate a host token and start the host:

```sh
export NYTE_TOKEN="$(node -e 'console.log(crypto.randomUUID())')"
printf '%s\n' "$NYTE_TOKEN"
node server.ts
```

#### Render the chat

Replace the generated `src/App.tsx`. Enter the token printed by the host to create a session.
The observer reads saved messages, follows streaming text, and reconnects when the watch breaks.

```tsx title="chat-web/src/App.tsx"
import { createNyteClient, livePartKey, SessionObserver, turnPartId } from "@nyte-ai/client";
import type { SessionState, UserTurnPart } from "@nyte-ai/client";
import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react";

function messageText(content: UserTurnPart["content"]) {
  return typeof content === "string"
    ? content
    : content.map((part) => (part.type === "text" ? part.text : "")).join("");
}

export default function App() {
  const [token, setToken] = useState("");
  const [sessionId, setSessionId] = useState<SessionState["sessionId"]>();
  const [state, setState] = useState<SessionState>();
  const [input, setInput] = useState("");
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [connectionError, setConnectionError] = useState("");
  const [submitError, setSubmitError] = useState("");
  const sdk = useMemo(() => createNyteClient({ baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:8787", token }), [token]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (sessionId === undefined) return;
    let closed = false;
    const observer = new SessionObserver(sdk, {
      sessionId,
      onError: (cause) => {
        if (!closed) setConnectionError(cause.message);
      },
    });
    const unsubscribe = observer.subscribe((update) => {
      setState(update.state);
      setConnectionError("");
    });
    void observer.start().catch((cause: unknown) => {
      if (!closed) setConnectionError(cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause));
    });
    return () => {
      closed = true;
      unsubscribe();
      observer.close();
    };
  }, [sdk, sessionId]);

  async function submit() {
    setBusy(true);
    setSubmitError("");
    try {
      if (sessionId === undefined) {
        const session = await sdk.sessions.create();
        setSessionId(session.sessionId);
        return;
      }
      if (!input.trim()) return;
      await sdk.messages.send({
        sessionId,
        content: input,
        key: crypto.randomUUID(),
        delivery: "next",
      });
      setInput("");
    } catch (cause) {
      setSubmitError(cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause));
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Chat</h1>
      {state?.transcript.items.map((turn) =>
        turn.kind === "turn" ? (
          <section key={turn.id}>
            {turn.parts.map((part) =>
              part.kind === "user" || part.kind === "assistant" ? (
                <p key={turnPartId(part)} style={{ whiteSpace: "pre-wrap" }}>
                  <strong>{part.kind === "user" ? "You: " : "AI: "}</strong>
                  {part.kind === "user" ? messageText(part.content) : part.text}
                </p>
              ) : null,
            )}
            {turn.failure && <p role="alert">{JSON.stringify(turn.failure)}</p>}
          </section>
        ) : null,
      )}
      {state?.pending.map((item) => (
        <p key={item.change}>You: {messageText(item.content)} (queued)</p>
      ))}
      {state?.overlay.map((part) =>
        part.kind === "text" ? (
          <p key={livePartKey(part)} style={{ whiteSpace: "pre-wrap" }}>
            AI: {part.text}
          </p>
        ) : null,
      )}
      {connectionError && <p role="alert">Connection: {connectionError}</p>}
      {submitError && <p role="alert">{submitError}</p>}
      <form
        onSubmit={(event) => {
          event.preventDefault();
          void submit();
        }}
      >
        {sessionId === undefined ? (
          <label>
            Host token
            <input
              type="password"
              value={token}
              disabled={busy}
              onChange={(event) => setToken(event.target.value)}
              required
              minLength={16}
            />
          </label>
        ) : (
          <label>
            Message
            <input
              value={input}
              disabled={busy || state === undefined}
              onChange={(event) => setInput(event.target.value)}
              required
            />
          </label>
        )}
        <button disabled={busy || (sessionId !== undefined && state === undefined)}>
          {sessionId === undefined ? "Start chat" : "Send"}
        </button>
      </form>
    </main>
  );
}
```

In another terminal, from `chat-web`:

```sh
pnpm dev --host localhost --port 5173 --strictPort
```

Open `http://localhost:5173`. The host stores conversation history, so the browser sends only the
new message, not the whole transcript. This example creates a new session each time you start a
chat. Save the returned `sessionId` to reopen that session after a reload.

This text-only example leaves out tool rendering and optimistic sends. A failed send can have
reached the host even if its receipt was lost. For automatic retries under the same key and
immediate pending messages, use `createOutbox` as shown in [Make a TUI](#make-a-tui).

### Next.js

Keep the same host running. In a separate directory, create a standalone Next.js app, choose the
App Router without a `src` directory, and install only the browser client:

```sh
pnpm create next-app chat-next
cd chat-next
pnpm add @nyte-ai/client@next
```

Copy the Vite `App.tsx` to `chat-next/app/page.tsx` and add `"use client";` before its imports.
Keep the generated root layout and Next config. The public release will ship compiled JavaScript
and type declarations, so it will not need `transpilePackages`.

```sh
pnpm dev --hostname localhost --port 3000
```

Open `http://localhost:3000` and enter the same host token. There is no Next.js API route in this
version. Both frontends call the same long-running host, which owns execution and storage.
Moving `sdk.attach()` into a serverless request handler would not keep it running after the
request ends. For that deployment model, start with the
[Vercel Workflow demo](https://github.com/interfaces-lab/nyte/blob/main/packages/demo/server/vercel/README.md).

### Before deploying

The loopback URLs and token entry above are for local development. For a deployed frontend, use
an HTTPS host URL and allow its exact origin in `browserOrigins`. Never put provider credentials
or a shared host token in `VITE_*` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables; those values go into the browser
bundle. The local token grants full access to this host, not just one session. A multi-user app
needs server-side authentication and session permissions through
[`createNyteServer`](https://github.com/interfaces-lab/nyte/blob/main/packages/server/README.md#permissions-for-remote-clients).
Nyte's SDK protocol is not the AI SDK UI message protocol, so `useChat` needs an adapter rather
than pointing directly at these endpoints.

## Make a TUI

Keep the host and render the session yourself. `@nyte-ai/client` gives you a `SessionObserver`, a
live view of the session, and an outbox, which holds the messages the user has typed but the store
hasn't confirmed yet.

```ts title="tui.ts"
import { createOutbox, SessionObserver } from "@nyte-ai/client";
import type { OutboxRow, SessionState } from "@nyte-ai/client";

const observer = new SessionObserver(sdk, { sessionId });
const outbox = createOutbox({ send: (input) => sdk.messages.send(input) });

const draw = (state: SessionState, rows: readonly OutboxRow[]) =>
  console.log(state.transcript.items.length, "turns,", rows.length, "pending");

observer.subscribe((update) => {
  outbox.observe(update);
  draw(update.state, outbox.rows());
});
outbox.subscribe(() => {
  if (observer.state !== undefined) draw(observer.state, outbox.rows());
});

await observer.start();
await outbox.submit({ sessionId, content: "Explain this repository", delivery: "next" });
```

The SDK never retries. The observer handles reading: it takes a snapshot, follows live events, and
starts over from a fresh snapshot when the watch breaks. The outbox handles writing: it shows the
message the moment the user hits enter, retries under one idempotency key until the send lands, and
drops its copy once the observer sees the real one.

`delivery: "next"` queues the message for when the agent is idle. `"steer"` delivers it at the next
response boundary while the agent is still working. For messages that should survive a restart,
give the outbox a `storage` and call `activate()` on startup. The shipped TUI wires these the same
way in
[`packages/tui/src/interactive.ts`](https://github.com/interfaces-lab/nyte/blob/main/packages/tui/src/interactive.ts).

## Or extend what's already there

To change part of the TUI, write a plugin. Its rendering, transcript, and composer are internal.
Through `@nyte-ai/plugin` you can add tools to sessions, listen to session events, show toasts, and
render into the `session.composer.top` slot.

## What there is to copy

| Path                              | What runs                                                          |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `packages/demo/server/cloudflare` | Local SQLite-backed Durable Object with alarm-driven execution     |
| `packages/demo/server/vercel`     | PostgreSQL-backed chat host with durable Vercel Workflow execution |
| `packages/demo/website`           | Static interface previews, not a live agent                        |

The server demos are chat only, with no workspace or terminal. Setup is in the
[Cloudflare guide](https://github.com/interfaces-lab/nyte/blob/main/packages/demo/server/cloudflare/README.md)
and the [Vercel guide](https://github.com/interfaces-lab/nyte/blob/main/packages/demo/server/vercel/README.md).
